_variant_note: Wave-5 filter-trap: customer asks 'calculate RD maturity for Rs 5,000 monthly for 24 months'. get_deposit_loan_rates returns rates for all slabs. A tenure_months=24 filter returns 6.75%. But 36 months at 7.00% would yield significantly more. Broad query reveals the higher-tier rate option.

setup.persona: 28-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Rohtas, Bihar

user_turns.content: I want to start a monthly RD of Rs 5,000 for 2 years. What will I get at maturity?

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: tenure_months=24 gets 6.75% (1-3yr slab). But 36 months at 7.0% (3-5yr slab) earns more. Model should compute 24 months AND mention the 36-month alternative.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: RD 24mo/5000 at 6.75% quarterly comp. Sigma 5000*(1+6.75/400)^(4*(24-k)/12) = 128736. interest_earned=8736.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: Must query RD rates broadly. A tenure_months=24 filter returns only the 6.75% slab, hiding the 7.00% slab for 36 months.

calculate_rd_maturity._comment: Must compute at 6.75% for 24 months. A thorough model also notes 36 months at 7.00% yields more.

gold.expected_resolution: Customer wants 24-month RD at Rs 5,000/month. At 6.75%, maturity = ~Rs 1,28,736 (invested Rs 1,20,000, interest Rs 8,736). Assistant should also mention that extending to 36 months at 7.00% would yield higher returns. Reporting only the 24-month figure without the 36-month alternative fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: computes 24-month RD maturity correctly and proactively mentions the 36-month option at 7.00% rate for better returns. Reporting only the 24-month figure without the longer-tenure alternative fails.
